desc:
Choose exactly k elements of nums, keeping their original order, so that the chosen sequence is as small as possible in lexicographic order. Sequences are compared element by element from the left; the first position where they differ decides, and the one with the smaller value there is smaller.

Return that smallest subsequence. Example: nums = [3, 5, 2, 6] and k = 2 gives [2, 6].
hints: Compare candidate answers: the very first element matters most, so you want the smallest possible first element. How far to the right can the first element sit and still leave room for k-1 more?

Deleting n - k elements is the same as choosing k. When a new element is smaller than the last kept one, removing the last kept one makes the sequence smaller, as long as enough elements remain to still reach length k.

Keep a stack. For each element at index i, pop while the top is larger than it and len(stack) - 1 + (n - i) ≥ k (so after the pop there are still enough elements left). Push the element if the stack has fewer than k items. The stack is the answer.
editorial: This is the 'remove digits to make the smallest number' greedy on arbitrary values. Process the elements left to right and keep a stack that is the best sequence found so far. If the current value is smaller than the top and we can afford to drop the top (the elements still unread plus the stack minus one are enough to fill k slots), dropping it can only make the sequence lexicographically smaller, because the current value now takes an earlier position.

After the pops, push the current element only if the stack has fewer than k elements; otherwise the element is discarded, since a full stack that could not be improved by it must be kept as is. Every element enters and leaves the stack at most once, so the time is O(n) and the space O(k).
